newsitem.title: INDIA: Landmine blast kills four in India - news agency.
newsitem.headline: Landmine blast kills four in India - news agency.

text.p: Four political activists were killed and several injured on Tuesday when suspected leftwing militants set off a landmine in the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

The news agency quoted police as saying a group of Congress party workers were travelling in a jeep to a party meeting when members of the outlawed People's War Group, a Maoist militant organisation, triggered the blast.
The People's War Group (PWG) is part of the Naxalite movement, which was started in India in the 1960s by groups that split from the main communist party.
The PWG is considered the most violent of the Naxalite outfits and controls large forest tracts straddling the states of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Orissa.
Naxalites, who reject the Indian government and want to set up a Maoist state of their own, killed 202 civilians and 45 policemen in Andhra Pradesh last year, according to state authorities.
